header.title: Idea library
header.subtitle: Well-known chart-reading methods, explained in plain words. Learn an idea, then try it as a scan.
frame: Education, not advice. Each idea is a general method explained in plain words; ATP does not tell you what to trade or when.
No results are claimed. Nothing here says how well an idea has done or will do.
Every number is your own setting. You choose the instruments, the settings and every decision; anything you run is on paper.
header.adopt_later: Using an idea as a paper strategy comes later, once ATP's strategy templates carry it. You will set every value yourself, and it will run on paper only.

beginner.title: Not sure where to start?
beginner.intro: Answer three questions and we suggest two or three ideas to read first. This is a reading list, not advice.

questions.text: Do you prefer to follow a trend or to work inside a range?
How often can you look at your charts?

options.label: A few times a day or less

questions.text: Do you write option spreads (as an option seller)?

ideas.name: Trend pullback to demand or supply
ideas.one_line: In a trend, wait for price to pull back into an area where the trend started before, and watch how it reacts there.
ideas.works_best_when: The higher timeframe shows a clear trend and the pullback is slow and overlapping.
ideas.tends_to_fail_when: The trend is already turning, or the pullback is fast and strong instead of tired.
plain: Trends rarely move in a straight line. After a push, price usually rests and pulls back before the next push.
This idea waits for that pullback to reach a demand area in an uptrend, or a supply area in a downtrend: a place where buyers or sellers stepped in strongly before.

Inside the area you watch for a reaction: a candle that rejects the area, or a small change of character on a lower timeframe. The idea is wrong if price moves clearly beyond the far side of the area.

logic.context: A trend on the higher timeframe (your setting; Daily for a 15-minute chart by default).
logic.area: The nearest valid demand area in an uptrend, or supply area in a downtrend, that price is now visiting.
logic.trigger: A rejection or commitment candle inside the area, or a change of character on a lower timeframe inside the area.
logic.invalidation: Price moves beyond the far edge of the area.
evidence: The pullback looks corrective: overlapping candles, smaller bodies than the push, lighter volume.
A commitment candle on rising volume.
A change of character on a lower timeframe.
RSI divergence into the area.
The area lines up with a trendline or another level.

structure_words: Uptrend; the pullback reached a demand area; a handover is forming; a continuation setup formed.
Downtrend; the pullback reached a supply area; a handover is forming; a continuation setup formed.

settings.label: Trend swing size
settings.help: How big a swing must be to count when the trend is read. Bigger swings give a slower, steadier trend.

settings.label: How close counts as inside the area (%)
settings.help: How near price must be to a demand or supply area to count as visiting it.

your_decisions: Which instruments you look at.
The higher timeframe and the chart timeframe.
Whether you act on a setup at all, and on which side.
Lots, risk per trade and your exit rules, in your own paper bot settings.
ideas.provenance: A widely taught price-action idea (trend, pullback, demand and supply), written for ATP as a generic method. It is not any one person's private method, and no results are claimed for it.

scans.label: Uptrend version
scans.text: DowTrend($trend_degree)@1d == "UP" AND NearZone("demand", $area_tolerance_pct, "zones") AND (PatternBullish() OR StructureEvent() == "CHOCH_BULLISH")

scans.label: Downtrend version
scans.text: DowTrend($trend_degree)@1d == "DOWN" AND NearZone("supply", $area_tolerance_pct, "zones") AND (PatternBearish() OR StructureEvent() == "CHOCH_BEARISH")

ideas.scan_gaps: The scan reads the reaction on the scan's own timeframe; a lower-timeframe change of character and the area's own timeframe come later.

ideas.name: Range edges
ideas.one_line: When price moves sideways between two edges, watch for a rejection at the upper or lower edge.
ideas.works_best_when: Price has failed to make a new extreme on both sides several times and the edges are clear.
ideas.tends_to_fail_when: Price starts to close and hold beyond an edge: the range may be ending.
plain: A range is a market that has stopped trending: it keeps failing to make a new high and a new low.
The upper edge acts as a supply area and the lower edge as a demand area. This idea watches for a rejection at one of the edges.

A rejection can be a commitment candle, a lower-timeframe change of character, or a quick move beyond the edge that closes back inside. The idea is wrong when price accepts beyond the edge: a close beyond it and a new swing formed there.

logic.context: A range by structure: price fails to make a new extreme on both sides.
logic.area: The upper edge (supply) or the lower edge (demand).
logic.trigger: A rejection at the edge: a commitment candle, a lower-timeframe change of character, or a move beyond the edge that closes back inside.
logic.invalidation: Acceptance beyond the edge: a close beyond it and a swing formed beyond it.
evidence: The edge has been respected before.
RSI divergence at the edge.
Volume fades as price reaches the edge.

structure_words: Range; price at the upper edge; rejection formed.
Range; price at the lower edge; rejection formed.

settings.label: Swing size
settings.help: How big a swing must be to count when the range and its edges are read.

your_decisions: Which instruments you look at, and the chart timeframe.
Whether you act at an edge at all, and how.
Lots, risk per trade and your exit rules, in your own paper bot settings.
ideas.provenance: A widely taught idea of trading the edges of a sideways market, written for ATP as a generic method. No results are claimed for it.
ideas.scan_gaps: The scan reads the edge as the latest swing high or low; a lower-timeframe change of character comes later.

adopt.note: The paper strategy reads exactly this idea's scans, both edges. It counts the idea as wrong once price is beyond the edge itself; a swing formed beyond the edge is not checked yet.

ideas.name: RSI divergence at an area
ideas.one_line: Price pushes into an area to a new extreme, but RSI does not follow: the push may be running out of strength.
ideas.works_best_when: The push into the area is stretched and the divergence is clear between two pushes.
ideas.tends_to_fail_when: A strong trend keeps going: divergence can repeat several times before anything turns.
plain: RSI is a momentum gauge. When price makes a new high but RSI makes a lower high, momentum is not confirming the move. That is called a bearish divergence; the mirror image is a bullish divergence.
This idea only looks at divergence when price is pushing into a valid demand or supply area, and waits for a reaction after it.
The idea is wrong if price moves beyond the extreme of the push.

logic.area: A valid supply area (for bearish divergence) or demand area (for bullish divergence) that price pushes into.
logic.trigger: After the divergence, a change of character on a lower timeframe or a commitment candle.
logic.invalidation: Price moves beyond the extreme of the push.
evidence: Regular divergence between the consecutive pushes into the area.
The area has held before.
A clear change of character after the divergence.

structure_words: Price pushed into a supply area with bearish RSI divergence; a lower-timeframe change of character confirmed.
Price pushed into a demand area with bullish RSI divergence; a lower-timeframe change of character confirmed.

settings.label: How recent the divergence must be (bars)
settings.help: The latest swing of the divergence must be at most this many bars back.

settings.label: Swing size
settings.help: How big a swing must be to count as a push.

settings.label: How close counts as inside the area (%)
settings.help: How near price must be to a demand or supply area to count as inside it.

your_decisions: Which instruments you look at, and the chart timeframe.
Whether you act on a divergence at all.
Lots, risk per trade and your exit rules, in your own paper bot settings.
ideas.provenance: RSI divergence is a widely taught momentum idea; reading it only at demand and supply areas is a common price-action refinement. Written for ATP as a generic method. No results are claimed for it.

scans.label: Bearish divergence at supply
scans.text: RsiDivergence("bearish", $divergence_lookback, $swing_size) AND NearZone("supply", $area_tolerance_pct, "zones") AND (PatternBearish() OR StructureEvent() == "CHOCH_BEARISH")

scans.label: Bullish divergence at demand
scans.text: RsiDivergence("bullish", $divergence_lookback, $swing_size) AND NearZone("demand", $area_tolerance_pct, "zones") AND (PatternBullish() OR StructureEvent() == "CHOCH_BULLISH")

ideas.scan_gaps: The scan reads the reaction on the scan's own timeframe; a lower-timeframe change of character comes later.

ideas.name: Sweep and reclaim
ideas.one_line: Price runs just beyond an obvious high or low, then closes back inside: the move beyond may have been a trap.
ideas.works_best_when: The high or low is obvious to everyone and sits near or inside a demand or supply area.
ideas.tends_to_fail_when: Price keeps going after the sweep and the next push holds beyond the old extreme.
plain: Obvious highs and lows attract orders. Price often trades a little beyond them and then comes straight back.
This idea looks for that: a move beyond a prior swing high or low, near a supply or demand area, that closes back inside.
Then it waits for the next push to fail inside the extreme of the sweep. The idea is wrong if price moves beyond the sweep's extreme.

logic.context: Obvious liquidity, such as equal highs or lows or a prior swing extreme, near or inside an area.
logic.area: The supply area above (for a sweep of highs) or the demand area below (for a sweep of lows).
logic.trigger: The next push fails inside the extreme of the sweep.
logic.invalidation: Price moves beyond the extreme of the sweep.
evidence: The swept level was obvious (equal highs or lows, a clear prior swing).
A fast close back inside after the sweep.
The follow-up push is weaker than the sweep.

structure_words: Liquidity above the highs was swept and price closed back inside the supply area; the follow-up push failed.
Liquidity below the lows was swept and price closed back inside the demand area; the follow-up push failed.

settings.label: Swing size
settings.help: How big a swing must be to count as the high or low that gets swept.

settings.label: How close counts as inside the area (%)
settings.help: How near price must be to a demand or supply area to count as inside it.

your_decisions: Which instruments you look at, and the chart timeframe.
Whether the follow-up push really failed, and whether you act at all.
Lots, risk per trade and your exit rules, in your own paper bot settings.
ideas.provenance: The sweep (also called an upthrust or a spring) is a widely taught price-action idea, written for ATP as a generic method. No results are claimed for it.

scans.label: Sweep above the highs
scans.text: high > SwingHigh($swing_size) AND close < SwingHigh($swing_size) AND NearZone("supply", $area_tolerance_pct, "zones")

scans.label: Sweep below the lows
scans.text: low < SwingLow($swing_size) AND close > SwingLow($swing_size) AND NearZone("demand", $area_tolerance_pct, "zones")

ideas.scan_gaps: The scan finds the sweep and the close back inside. Equal highs or lows and the failed follow-up push come later; check them on the chart for now.

ideas.name: Breakout and retest
ideas.one_line: After a level breaks for real, wait for price to come back and test it from the other side.
ideas.works_best_when: The break was clean (a close beyond and a new swing beyond) and the return is calm.
ideas.tends_to_fail_when: Price slips back through the level and accepts on the old side.
plain: When an area or line breaks for real, its role often flips: old resistance can act as support, and old support as resistance.
This idea does not chase the break. It waits for price to return to the broken level from the other side, and looks for a rejection candle that closes away from it.
The idea is wrong if price accepts back through the level.

logic.context: An area or line broken by the method's definition: a close beyond it and a swing formed beyond it.
logic.area: The broken area or line, approached from the other side.
logic.trigger: A rejection candle that closes away from the level.
evidence: The break came with displacement (a strong candle).
The return to the level is slow and overlapping.
The rejection candle closes firmly away from the level.

structure_words: Former resistance was broken and is being retested from above; rejection formed.
Former support was broken and is being retested from below; rejection formed.

settings.label: What broke
settings.help: The kind of level whose retest you want to see.

settings.label: Retest within (bars)
settings.help: The return must come within this many bars after the break; a later return is a new base, not a retest.

your_decisions: Which instruments you look at, and the chart timeframe.
Whether you act on a retest at all.
Lots, risk per trade and your exit rules, in your own paper bot settings.
ideas.provenance: The retest of a broken level (a structure flip) is a widely taught idea, written for ATP as a generic method. It is a retest idea, never a breakout-chasing one. No results are claimed for it.
ideas.scan_gaps: The scan reads the break as a close beyond the level by a small set distance; a swing formed beyond the level is not checked yet.

adopt.note: The paper strategy reads exactly this idea's scans, both sides. It counts the idea as wrong once price is back through the level; a swing formed beyond the level is not checked yet.

ideas.name: Channel trading
ideas.one_line: In a rising or falling channel, watch for a rejection at the channel line on the trend's side.
ideas.works_best_when: Both channel lines have at least two clear reactions and the channel slopes steadily.
ideas.tends_to_fail_when: Price closes through the line and forms a swing beyond it: the channel is broken.
plain: A channel is two parallel lines that price has reacted to several times.
This idea only watches the line on the trend's side: the lower line in a rising channel, the upper line in a falling one. It waits for a rejection there.
The idea is wrong when price closes through the line and forms a swing beyond it. A broken channel can then become a breakout and retest (T5).

logic.context: A channel made of two parallel lines, each with at least two reactions, on the chart or a higher timeframe.
logic.area: The channel line in the trend's favour: the lower line in a rising channel, the upper line in a falling one.
logic.trigger: A rejection at the line: a commitment candle or a lower-timeframe change of character.
logic.invalidation: A close through the line and a swing formed beyond it.
evidence: Each line has clear earlier reactions.
The touch lines up with a demand or supply area.
RSI divergence at the line.

structure_words: Rising channel; price at the lower channel line; rejection formed.
Falling channel; price at the upper channel line; rejection formed.
your_decisions: Which instruments you look at, and the chart timeframe.
Whether you act at the line at all.
Lots, risk per trade and your exit rules, in your own paper bot settings.
ideas.provenance: Channel trading is a widely taught idea, written for ATP as a generic method. No results are claimed for it.
ideas.scan_gaps: A scan for this idea comes later: Find setups cannot yet tell when price is at a channel line.

ideas.name: Pattern at an area
ideas.one_line: A double top or bottom, or a head and shoulders, that forms at a valid demand or supply area.
ideas.works_best_when: The pattern is clean, built from clear swings, and sits at an area that has held before.
ideas.tends_to_fail_when: The neckline breaks but price comes straight back through it.
plain: Some swing patterns show a trend running out of strength: a double top or bottom, or a head and shoulders and its inverse.
This idea only counts them when they form at a valid demand or supply area.

It waits for the neckline to break and then for the retest to be rejected (as in T5), or for a lower-timeframe change of character at the second top or bottom (your choice). The idea is wrong if price moves beyond the pattern's extreme.

logic.context: A double top or bottom, or a head and shoulders (or its inverse), recognised from swings, at or from a valid area.
logic.area: The demand or supply area where the pattern forms.
logic.trigger: The neckline breaks and the retest is rejected, or a lower-timeframe change of character at the second top or bottom.
logic.invalidation: Price moves beyond the pattern's extreme.
evidence: The second push is weaker than the first.
RSI divergence between the tops or bottoms.
A clean neckline break.

structure_words: Double top formed at a supply area; the neckline broke and the retest was rejected.
Double bottom formed at a demand area; the neckline broke and the retest was rejected.

settings.label: Swing size
settings.help: How big a swing must be to count as a top or a bottom, and when the trend before the pattern is read.

settings.label: How close counts as inside the area (%)
settings.help: How near price must be to a demand or supply area to count as inside it.

your_decisions: Which instruments you look at, and the chart timeframe.
Which trigger you prefer: the neckline retest or the lower-timeframe change of character.
Lots, risk per trade and your exit rules, in your own paper bot settings.
ideas.provenance: Double tops and bottoms and head and shoulders are classic chart patterns from public technical-analysis books, written for ATP as a generic method. No results are claimed for them.
ideas.scan_gaps: The scan finds the second top or bottom: after a rise (or a fall), price comes back to the last swing high (or low), rejects it on the scan's own timeframe, at a supply (or demand) area. Head and shoulders and the neckline break with its retest come later.

ideas.name: Options seller pack
ideas.one_line: The trend pullback and range edge ideas, reduced to the direction of the structure, for people who write option spreads.
ideas.works_best_when: You already have your own options construction and only want to know the structure's direction.
ideas.tends_to_fail_when: The structure changes quickly, for example a range that breaks soon after a signal.
plain: Option writers often care about one thing: is the structure a bullish continuation, a bearish continuation, or a range with price at an edge?
This pack bundles the trend pullback (T1) and range edges (T2) ideas and reports only that direction, with the area and the invalidation area.

What each signal type leads to, if anything, is your own decision in your paper bot settings: the construction, strikes, width, lots, expiry rule and exits. The pack never names a strike, a premium or a lot.

logic.context: The trend pullback idea (T1) and the range edges idea (T2); the channel idea (T6) can join later.
logic.area: The area from the idea that formed the signal.
logic.invalidation: The invalidation of that idea, shown as an area.
evidence: The signal type: bullish continuation, bearish continuation, range upper edge or range lower edge.
The evidence of the idea that formed it.

structure_words: Bullish continuation; the pullback reached a demand area; a handover is forming.
Range upper edge; price at the upper edge; rejection formed.

settings.label: Trend swing size
settings.help: How big a swing must be to count when the trend is read.

settings.label: How close counts as inside the area (%)
settings.help: How near price must be to a demand or supply area to count as visiting it.

settings.label: Range swing size
settings.help: How big a swing must be to count when the range and its edges are read.

your_decisions: Which underlyings you look at, and the chart timeframe.
What each signal type leads to, if anything: your construction, strikes, width, lots, expiry rule and exits, all in your own paper bot settings.
Whether you act on a signal at all.
ideas.provenance: A bundle of the trend pullback and range edges ideas in this library, reduced to the structure's direction. Written for ATP as a generic method. No results are claimed for it.

scans.label: Bullish continuation
scans.text: DowTrend($trend_degree)@1d == "UP" AND NearZone("demand", $area_tolerance_pct, "zones") AND (PatternBullish() OR StructureEvent() == "CHOCH_BULLISH")

scans.label: Bearish continuation
scans.text: DowTrend($trend_degree)@1d == "DOWN" AND NearZone("supply", $area_tolerance_pct, "zones") AND (PatternBearish() OR StructureEvent() == "CHOCH_BEARISH")

ideas.scan_gaps: Each signal type is its own scan for now; one combined view comes later.
